Large files open straight away and stay light, images and PDFs fit the
window, and Quick Open goes where you type. This release also brings the
Typst package fix from 0.1.12, which was never published. More at
[www.malgel.com](https://www.malgel.com).

## New

- **Large files open the way VS Code opens them.** A text file past 2 MB (or
  300,000 lines) opens without a question. Highlighting, the preview, the
  outline and spell checking are turned off, and an info bar above the
  editor says so. **Enable anyway** brings back the preview of the file's
  beginning and its outline without freezing the window. The text is kept
  once, and statistics are counted straight from the editor's text. A
  20 MB file now peaks at about 310 MB instead of 3.7 GB; a 100 MB file at
  about 740 MB instead of 11 GB.
- **Only truly huge or binary files ask first.** Text over 512 MiB, and files
  that look binary, ask whether to open them before anything is read. This
  applies from Quick Open, the Explorer, the command line, drag and drop
  and session restore.
- **Quick Open takes paths.** Typing a path (`docs/guide.md`, `src/main.rs:42`
  or a folder such as `build/`) opens it or lists it, even when `.gitignore`
  leaves it out of the search.
- **A Typst file that doesn't compile opens as source** and turns into its
  pages once it compiles.
- **`.txt` opens as plain text**, and a new file indents the way its language
  usually does.

## Fixed

- **Typst packages resolve, on every platform.** A `.typ` file that imports a
  package (`#import "@preview/touying:0.7.4": *`) previews. Packages are read
  from the folders the `typst` command uses, and a missing package is
  reported by its name.
- **Images fit the window.** A large picture or plot opens fitted to the
  viewer instead of cropped at its corner. A very large picture is kept at
  display resolution.
- **PDFs relayout** when the window or the sidebar changes size.
- The status bar names the language of a source file, and shows the size and
  zoom of an image or PDF.
- Files opened together from the command line keep the order they were given.
- The crash-recovery copy of a large document is written without holding the
  whole text twice, so typing stays light.

## Downloads

| System | File |
| --- | --- |
| macOS 11+ (Apple silicon) | `Malgel-0.1.13-macos-arm64.dmg`: open it and drag Malgel to Applications |
| Windows 10+ | `Malgel-0.1.13-windows-x64-setup.exe` (installer) or `Malgel-0.1.13-windows-x64.zip` (portable) |
| Linux x86_64 | `Malgel-0.1.13-x86_64.AppImage` (`chmod +x` it, then run it) or `malgel-0.1.13-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |

The macOS app is signed ad hoc and not notarized, so Gatekeeper blocks it after download: right-click it and choose Open once, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Malgel.app`. The Windows files are unsigned: SmartScreen may warn, and **More info → Run anyway** gets past it. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists every file's checksum.
